name: Riboflavin (vitamin B2)
short: Reviews describe riboflavin as unlikely to cause toxicity because excess is quickly eliminated; adverse events in migraine use are described as minimal.
text: A narrative review states that, because excess riboflavin is quickly eliminated from the body, it is unlikely to cause negative effects or toxicity in humans. A review of supplements for headache describes adverse events with riboflavin for migraine prevention in adults as minimal. These statements come from narrative reviews rather than pooled trial safety data. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.

quotes: Because of its physiological nature and fast elimination from the human body when in excess, riboflavin consumed is unlikely to induce any negative effects or develop toxicity in humans.
citations.label: Lee et al., 2023, Nutr Res
citations.title: Medicinal benefits, biological, and nanoencapsulation functions of riboflavin with its toxicity profile: A narrative review.

quotes: Riboflavin or vitamin B2 can be recommended for migraine prevention in adults, but pediatric use is not proven. Adverse events are minimal.
citations.label: Tepper et al., 2025, Curr Pain Headache Rep
citations.title: Nutraceuticals and Headache 2024: Riboflavin, Coenzyme Q10, Feverfew, Magnesium, Melatonin, and Butterbur.
